headline: Medium-risk pair: shared browser/network and file-handling create prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict pathways; no direct evidence of tighter isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests web content via browsers, files, and MCP, while Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. That creates a plausible path for attacker-controlled content from A to influence B if outputs are copied or synced through shared workspace or tickets. No direct shared-channel evidence is present, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A outputs are pasted into B issue descriptions or notes
IF B ingests uploaded files or hyperlinks from A without sanitization
IF a shared workspace or MCP bridge is configured between the agents
mitigations: Disable automatic import of A outputs into B
Strip instructions from copied web text before filing tickets
Use a separate staging folder for A-generated artifacts
Add a manual review step before B consumes A content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags on transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher reads local documents and handles multiple API secrets, while Plane can receive file uploads and store issues, tasks, notes, and files. If the pair shares a workspace or operator account, sensitive research material can flow from A into B’s persisted records. Plane is not shown to upload context by default, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or upload set
IF A processes local documents containing secrets or regulated data
IF B stores uploaded files or notes without redaction
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Redact secrets before uploading artifacts to B
Restrict B file uploads to non-sensitive documents
Rotate any exposed API keys after shared handling
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can read files, run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and install packages; B cannot write its own filesystem but can accept uploads and has broad network egress. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable filesystem or git/database writes, so direct write-write conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because shared orchestration is not described.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
IF an orchestrator grants B write access not shown in its profile
IF A installs packages into an environment B also uses
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent
Run A and B in separate containers
Avoid shared package environments
Lock any shared task state before handoff
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces research reports and citations, and B manages issues/tasks/roadmaps that could treat those outputs as authoritative. That creates a default handoff risk where unverified research from A becomes operational work in B. B’s issue-tracking role makes downstream action plausible, but not directly evidenced as automatic.
conditions: IF B imports A-generated reports into issues or tasks
IF B acts on citations from A without independent verification
IF A’s outputs are used as source-of-truth for planning
mitigations: Require human review before creating B tasks from A output
Mark A outputs as draft-only
Cross-check citations against original sources
Limit B to storing links, not conclusions
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A handles research queries, local documents, citations, and multiple external APIs with secrets; B stores issues, tasks, notes, files, and hyperlinks. The profiles do not specify residency or retention, but the pair can move potentially sensitive content into a separate system with different logging and retention behavior. Because the compliance posture is undocumented, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is included in A outputs
IF B retains uploaded files or notes longer than A’s source system
IF the deployment spans jurisdictions with different residency rules
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data into shared tickets
Set short retention on B artifacts
Document the data flow between A and B
Review vendor terms for both systems
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
